optimizer.report:
WHAT WAS DONE (all in the private copy at .../scratchpad/opt-kernel-conv-bitexact/src/core/k3_ops.c; /workspace copy untouched).

Change 1 (bf16 x precast): k3_matmul_bf16 now converts x to a heap double scratch (56 KB at in=7168) once per call, before the OMP region; the AVX2 inner loop replaces four per-row _mm256_cvtps_pd(x) with _mm256_loadu_pd. f32->f64 is exact, so identical bits enter the identical fmadd sequence. Scalar branch and the tail loop are byte-for-byte untouched; free() after the loop, k3_fatal_oom on allocation failure (project style).

Change 2 (bf16 batched widen): the weight side loads 8 bf16 per _mm_loadu_si128, widens with one _mm256_cvtepu16_epi32 + _mm256_slli_epi32(,16), then splits halves back to the existing v0..v3 cvtps_pd/fmadd chain in the same order. Same values, same IEEE ops, same order.

Change 3 (mxfp4 double LUT + x precast): added K3_E2M1_PAIR_D[256][2] (widened at init from the float pair table; E2M1 values exact in double), x precast to double per call (28 KB at in=3584). The scalar (#else) branch now expands the group into double wf[64] from the double LUT — bit-identical since (double)wf_float == PAIR_D entries.

Change 4 (mxfp4 SIMD nibble decode, AVX2 path): after changes 1-3 the mxfp4 line was FLAT (~1.80 vs 1.82 ms) — the wf[] stack round-trip (narrow stores feeding wide loads = store-forwarding stalls) dominated, not the cvtps_pd. So the AVX2 path now decodes 4 packed bytes -> 8 elements per iteration entirely in registers: split lo/hi nibbles, interleave to element order, _mm256_cvtepu8_epi32, two _mm256_shuffle_epi8 lookups over byte-2/byte-3 tables (K3_E2M1_B2/B3, built at init from K3_E2M1's own bit patterns; bytes 0-1 of every E2M1 f32 pattern are zero), shift/OR to rebuild the EXACT f32 bit patterns (including -0.0 for code 8), then the unchanged cvtps_pd -> fmadd v0/v1 chain. wf[] is gone from the AVX2 path; the sub-8 tail reads K3_E2M1_PAIR_D directly with the same nibble order. Accumulation order, lane partition, reduction trees, per-group scale multiply, and OMP pragmas all unchanged. This took mxfp4 from ~1.80 to ~0.98 ms.

MEASUREMENT METHODOLOGY / CAVEAT: a sibling agent session shares this 4-core box and intermittently ran k3_model/k3 at ~300% CPU, inflating some runs 3x. I therefore built a baseline bench binary from HEAD and ran strictly interleaved base/new pairs, reporting medians over quiet rounds only (~30 quiet samples per side). Quiet medians: bf16 8.47 -> 6.50 ms (1.30x), mxfp4 1.79 -> 0.98 ms (1.83x). Disturbed rounds were discarded on both sides symmetrically.

ACCEPTANCE: (1) native AVX2 build: FNV1a bf16=d65cab2d141bb3b8, mxfp4=a231061237b5579d on every one of >20 runs at OMP_NUM_THREADS=4. (2) make test: 22 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped (tokenizer NOT RUN expected); also 22/0/0 on the ARCH='' scalar build. (3) ./bin/k3_model tests/fixtures: 32/32, 20/20, 20/20, "ENGINE MATCHES THE REFERENCE EXACTLY" (native and scalar builds). (4) CI pin ARCH='-mavx2 -mfma': both hashes exact. Scalar (no-AVX2) build: mxfp4 hash exact (a231061237b5579d), proving the change-3 scalar edits are consistent; the scalar bf16 bench hash is 243d616fa5952a37, but I verified the UNMODIFIED baseline scalar build prints the identical 243d616fa5952a37 — a pre-existing scalar-vs-AVX2 divergence caused by the bench's random uint16 weights containing bf16 NaN patterns whose payloads propagate differently through libm fma() vs vfmadd (test_ops's adversarial bf16 test compares scalar-vs-fp32 within one build and passes in both builds). My change moved no bit in any build: every build's hashes equal the corresponding baseline build's hashes.

FAILED ATTEMPT WORTH NOTING: changes 1-3 alone left mxfp4 at ~0-1% gain (double wf doubled the stack-buffer store/load traffic, cancelling the cvt savings); change 4 was necessary for the mxfp4 win.

RESIDUAL RISKS: (a) per-call malloc/free in both kernels — negligible at model sizes but adds ~1 us to tiny calls; (b) the pshufb decode relies on E2M1 f32 patterns having zero low 16 bits, which is a property of the value set (max 2 mantissa bits) and is derived at init from K3_E2M1 itself, so a future table edit that violates it would break silently — the FNV gate and test_expert would catch it; (c) accumulation order is provably unchanged everywhere, so no test noticed any difference (FNV hashes identical before/after in all builds).

optimizer.report:
WHAT WAS DONE. Replaced the scalar bf16->fp32 widen loop in k3_bind_layer_mem (src/model/k3_bind.c) with a static helper widen_bf16(): AVX2 path (_mm_loadu_si128 of 8 u16 -> _mm256_cvtepu16_epi32 -> _mm256_slli_epi32(...,16) -> _mm256_storeu_si256, scalar k3_bf16f tail for n%8) guarded by #if defined(__AVX2__), with the original scalar loop as the else-branch, and '#pragma omp parallel for schedule(static) if (n > 65536)' over disjoint index chunks in both branches. No other file touched; name resolution, bind ordering, alignment, and error paths unchanged. include/k3/k3.h, src/core/k3_ops.c, src/io/k3_trunk.c untouched (verified via git diff --stat).

EXACTNESS. Standalone memcmp harness (scratchpad, not committed) compared the helper against the reference scalar loop over all 65536 u16 values at lengths 65529..65536 (all tail residues) and over 6.42M-element random buffers at 4 odd lengths above the OMP threshold: byte-identical in every case. No float arithmetic exists in the path (pure 16-bit shift), so there is no accumulation-order concern. bench_kernels FNV hashes unchanged (bf16=d65cab2d141bb3b8, mxfp4=a231061237b5579d).

ACCEPTANCE. (1) make test: 22 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped. (2) ./bin/k3_model tests/fixtures: VERDICT ENGINE MATCHES THE REFERENCE EXACTLY, 32/32 + 20/20 + 20/20 + 20/20. (3) bench hashes unchanged as above. (4) End-to-end: built a tiny checkpoint (python3 tools/make_tiny_checkpoint.py; tools/pack_trunk.py with n_layers=13 — the default 93 fails on the 13-layer tiny model) and ran ./bin/k3 tinyck --trunk tinytrunk --ids 1,2,3 --gen 8 --trunk-gb 1 --cache-gb 1 at OMP_NUM_THREADS=4, 5 runs per arm against a stashed-baseline binary: emitted token ids byte-identical across all 10 runs (single unique md5: tokens 192,149,129,254,48,156,38,23). The tiny checkpoint's tensors are 128-wide, so its k3_trunk_widen_wall prints 0.00 s in both arms (%.2f format) — the counter comparison is unresolvable at tiny scale, so per the work order's fallback the performance number comes from a scratch microbenchmark of the exact shipped helper at the real router-gate size (6,422,528 elements): scalar median ~1.72-1.85 ms vs AVX2+OMP median ~0.50-0.78 ms at OMP_NUM_THREADS=4, median speedup 3.0x across 5 runs.

WHAT FAILED / NOTES. (a) The AVX2 intrinsics alone give ~0% over scalar here because gcc -O3 -march=native already auto-vectorizes the trivial shift loop; the win is almost entirely the OpenMP fan-out, bounded by memory bandwidth on this 4-core VM (3x, not the hoped 4-8x; a machine with more cores/bandwidth should do better, and the intrinsics guarantee vectorization when auto-vec fails). (b) One early measurement window showed the OMP path at 8 ms (slower than scalar) — this was transient scheduler/contention noise on the shared Firecracker box (load avg later hit 2.2 from external work and even bench_kernels' untouched kernels tripled); repeated runs are stable at 0.5-0.8 ms. Residual risk: on a heavily oversubscribed host, the parallel region can be slower than serial for one call; the if(n > 65536) clause limits this exposure to the large-matrix binds only. (c) make portable builds cleanly (scalar else-branch, pragma still active since portable keeps -fopenmp), and the native build has zero warnings.

optimizer.report:
WHAT WAS DONE. Memoized k3_trunk_bind results per pinned layer and per ring slot, exactly as the work order specified, confined to src/io/k3_trunk.{c,h}.

PRECONDITION VERIFIED FIRST. Read k3_bind_layer_mem (src/model/k3_bind.c:320-443): in the mem path it allocates nothing (b->blob stays NULL); every pointer in the produced K3LayerBind targets either the slot's raw run bytes or the slot's OWN widen area (base + aligned nbytes), both of which persist per pinned layer / per ring slot until that slot is reloaded. Not shared scratch, so full memoization (resolution + widen) is safe. The only self-referential pointers are b->lay.kda/mla/moe, which point into the K3LayerBind struct itself; the copy-out helper bind_from_memo() re-aims them at the caller's copy after the value copy. Also verified the caller (src/cli/k3_run.c:493-506) receives a value copy and mutates only its copy (moe.src/layer/cache_only), so the memo cannot be corrupted by the caller.

DESIGN. New K3Trunk fields: pin_bind[npin]+pin_bind_ok[npin], slot_bind[nslot]+slot_bind_layer[nslot] (~a few hundred bytes each). Invalidation at every point slot bytes change: (a) pinned first-touch load clears pin_bind_ok before load_run; (b) the sync ring-claim in k3_trunk_bind clears slot_bind_layer at the same instant layer_of is set -1, before the read; (c) k3_trunk_prefetch clears it before handing the slot to the reader thread. Memo is stored only after k3_bind_layer_mem returns 0; failures stay invalid. Every cache hit runs assert(memo->layer == L) (asserts are live: build has no -DNDEBUG). Memo arrays are touched only on the main thread; the IO thread only runs load_run.

MEASUREMENTS. (1) make test: 22 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped, including test_cache; ./bin/k3_model verdict "ENGINE MATCHES THE REFERENCE EXACTLY". (2) Tiny checkpoint (tools/make_tiny_checkpoint.py + pack_trunk.py, 13 layers), OMP_NUM_THREADS=4, 200 generated tokens, 5 runs per arm. Pinned arm (--trunk-gb 1, 13/13 pinned): widen wall median 0.02 s baseline (0.02/0.02/0.02/0.02/0.03) -> 0.00 s in ALL five runs after the change, over 2600 binds; bind wall median 0.02 -> 0.01 s. This is the work order's acceptance signature (widen drops to near zero after the first token). Token ids byte-identical to baseline in every run. (3) Streaming arm (--trunk-gb 0.001, deterministic hit rate 15.4%, ring invalidation exercised every token including the async prefetch path): token ids byte-identical to baseline and to the pinned arm in every run; widen for streamed layers correctly still paid (bytes change every token). (4) bench_kernels FNV hashes unchanged (bf16 d65cab2d141bb3b8, mxfp4 a231061237b5579d); kernel timings unchanged within noise, as expected for untouched kernel code.

HONEST CAVEATS. No arithmetic is performed or reordered — the hit path serves the exact same bytes/pointers, so output is bit-identical by construction and confirmed empirically. End-to-end s/token on the TINY checkpoint did not measurably change (bind is ~0.1% of tiny-model runtime and run-to-run noise on this shared box is 15-30%, including one 376 s outlier run); the multi-GB/token widen saving this targets only materializes at real checkpoint dimensions (26 MB widen per MoE layer, 90/93 pinned = ~2.3 GB/token), which cannot be run here. Success=true is claimed on the work order's own measurement gate (widen breakdown to near zero, tokens exact in all four configurations), not on a kernel-median improvement. Residual risk: any FUTURE code path that writes into a pinned buffer or ring slot without going through load_run's existing claim points must also clear the corresponding memo; the debug assert on every hit and the pessimistic claim-time invalidation are the guards.
